P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020
Author: M.Satyanarayana Murthy

entities.text: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Bench: M.Satyanarayana Murthy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice M.Satyanarayana Murthy
 Writ Petition Nos. 2259 And 2273 Of 2020
Common Order:

Both these writ petitions are filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by two different petitioners by names R. Venkateswarlu and P. Vasanth Reddy, questioning the orders of suspension of 2B License issued by the third respondent/The Deputy Commissioner of Prohibition & Excise,
Ananthapuram in Rc.No.391/2019/C1 dated 27.01.2020, challenged in these two writ petitions on identical grounds and therefore, I find it expedient to decide both these writ petitions by common order.
Since, the question involved in both these writ petitions is one and the same, W.P.No.2259 of 2020 is taken as leading case.

The petitioner obtained Form-2B License to run Bar & Restaurant under the provisions of Andhra Pradesh (Grant of Licensee of Selling by Bar and Conditions of License) Rules, 2017 (for short 'The Rules, 2017').

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh (Grant of Licensee of Selling by Bar and Conditions of License) Rules, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Ever since the date of grant of license, the petitioner was conducting business in the name and style of Chandu Restaurant and Bar at Kadiri without contravening any of the provisions of the A.P. Excise Act, 1968 (for short 'The Act') and the Rules, 2017 framed therein.

While the matter stood thus, the third respondent herein issued a show cause notice on 21.12.2019 alleging that the fourth respondent/Prohibition & Excise Superintendent submitted a report stating that the Station House Officer, Kadiri submitted a report stating that on 14.10.2019 at about 11:45 p.m (23:45 hrs), the Station House Officer, Kadiri along with staff conducted surprise inspection of the bar premises and collected two loose liquor bottles and checked the strength of the liquor and it was MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 found to be 26.4% and 25.4 up.
The bottles were sent for chemical examination and the chemical analysis report shown as 26.0 and 26.7 and found that the liquor was diluted.

Basing on the said report, the fourth respondent opined that the petitioner has willfully violated the provisions of Section 36(1)(b) & (c) of the Act r/w Rules 27, 33 and 37 of the Rules, 2017 and the third respondent directed the petitioner to submit explanation within seven (7)
days from the date of receipt of the notice.

As the offence alleged against the petitioner is purely technical in nature, the petitioner has not submitted any explanation within stipulated time and wanted to submit the explanation in the last week of the month and the same was not accepted on the ground that the period prescribed is already over.

It is also further contended that, third respondent herein passed the impugned order suspending the P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/
1 license, pending enquiry and that the action of the third respondent in suspending the license pending enquiry is not legal and the same is arbitrary; that the power to suspend the license is conferred on the third respondent under Section 31 of the Act.

entities.text: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A reading of Section 31 of the Act, it is clear that the licensing authority is given the discretion to either suspend or cancel a license.

It is submitted that the discretion has to be exercised by the third respondent taking into consideration,
the seriousness of the allegations made against the licensee.

A reading of the impugned order, it is clear that the only allegation against the petitioner is that the liquor strength is 26.4 and 25.4; that once the cap of the liquor bottle is opened, due to atmosphere condition also there would be a change in the strength of the liquor.
The variation in the strength of the liquor by the manufacturer would be around 1 to 2 % and normally the change is not taken as a violation.

MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 Similarly, the allegation made against the petitioner in W.P.No.2273 of 2020 is that, the strength of the liquor in respect of one bottle is 26.0 up instead of 24.9, the same is diluted in Indian made liquor.

The specific contention of the petitioners in both the writ petitions is that, variation of liquor is very minimal and the third respondent without exercising the discretion conferred on it, mechanically passed the orders impugned in these writ petitions, pending enquiry.

Hence, the orders are illegal,
arbitrary and in violative of principles of natural justice.

It is further contended that the orders passed by the third respondent is not disclosing any reason for suspension of the Bar License and it is contrary to the principle laid down by the Full Bench of this Court in Tappers Co-operative Society, Maddur v. Superintendent of Excise, Mahaboobnagar1,
wherein this Court in paragraph 45 of the judgment held that the power of suspension, pending enquiry cannot be exercised in a routine manner and unless that the suspension is necessary.

entities.text: Tappers Co-operative Society, Maddur v. Superintendent of Excise, Mahaboobnagar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that the observations of the Full Bench are directly applicable to the facts of the case and on the strength of the principle laid down in the judgment referred supra, the petitioners specifically contended that the original Rules, 2017 were repealed by Rules, 2019.
Therefore, the third respondent passed the order referring the Rules, 2017 and on this technical ground also, the impugned orders are liable to be set-aside.
It is specifically contended that, Section 2(21) of the Act defines 'liquor' and it includes today.
In so far as the Excise Act and the Bar 1984 (2) APLJ (HC) 1 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 Rules do not prescribe the procedure for collecting sample from the license premises.

Rule 27 of the A.P. Excise (Grant of License to Sell Toddy, Conditions of License and Taping of Excise Trees) Rules,
2017 provide the procedure for drawl of samples.

entities.text:
A.P. Excise (Grant of License to Sell Toddy, Conditions of License and Taping of Excise Trees) Rules,
2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per Rule 27 of the above Rules, three samples have to be collected and one sample should be kept with the license and one sample should be sent to the Court of competent jurisdiction and one sample should be sent for chemical examination.

The said procedure is prescribed as adulteration of liquor would entail criminal consequences and the accused would be given an opportunity to request the authorities to send the second sample for chemical examination.
In the present case, the authorities did not follow the Rules and have taken the entire bottle and sent the same for chemical examination.
By reason of the same, the petitioner is deprived of an opportunity to seek sending the second sample for chemical examination.

Hence, it is contended that the action of the respondents is illegal and arbitrary and the impugned orders are P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/
2 liable to be set-aside on this ground alone.
It is also contended that the petitioners have paid license fee and they are entitled for refund of the license fee for the period during which the petitioners have conducted business.

entities.text: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended that the allegations made against these petitioners are nto so grave which warrant the order of suspension.

Even the show cause notices issued by the third respondent fixing seven days time for submission of the explanation is contrary to the law laid down by the learned Single Judge of High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh2,
where the High Court held that, 15 days time is reasonable time for 2013 (6) ALD 247 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 submitting an explanation from the date of service of notice.

entities.text: High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On this ground also, the petitioners requested to set-aside the impugned orders in these writ petitions.
The respondents did not file any counter, but advanced arguments.

During hearing, learned counsel for the petitioners Sri O. Manohar Reddy has drawn the attention of this Court to Rule 46 for lifting samples to contend that the person who lifted the samples is incompetent to lift the samples and therefore, the very lifting of samples is illegal, since it is in violation of the Rules, 2017.

Even otherwise, as per Rule 27 of the A.P. Excise (Grant of License to Sell Toddy, Conditions of License and Taping of Excise Trees) Rules, 2017, three samples have to be collected and one sample should be kept with the license and one sample should be sent to the Court of competent jurisdiction and one sample should be sent to chemical examination.

entities.text: A.P. Excise (Grant of License to Sell Toddy, Conditions of License and Taping of Excise Trees) Rules, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Instead of following such procedure, due to absence of any such Rule for lifting of samples of liquor in the bar,
the fourth respondent adopted a short cut method and sent the entire bottle by lifting the sample,
thereby the petitioners were deprived of their right to make application(s) for referring the samples to chemical examination.
This amounts to denial of opportunity to prove their innocence, since adulteration of liquor leads to criminal prosecution having its serious consequences, involving issue of life and liberty.

Even as per Food Adulteration Act, Food Inspector is entitled to lift the samples as per the Food Safety Standard Act, the Food Inspector is entitled to take samples following necessary procedure prescribed under the Act.

Even they also can lift the samples from Bar & Restaurant, but they are required to follow the procedure MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 prescribed either under Food Adulteration Act, if the samples were drawn under the Food Adulteration Act and on account of repeal, the Food Inspector has to draw the samples by following the procedure prescribed under Food Safety Standard Act and Rules framed there under.

If the samples were drawn by the Food Inspector, the petitioners will have an opportunity to prove their innocence by making a request to send the other sample handed over to the Court for chemical examination.
But, on account of lack of sufficient clear procedure under the Rules, the petitioners are being suffered on account of suspension of license and therefore, requested to set-aside the same.

Whereas, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Prohibition & Excise would contend that the petitioners were given an opportunity to submit their explanation within seven days, but they did not avail their opportunity and they cannot be prohibited to submit their explanation leisurely as and when they find time, on this ground alone, the request of the petitioners is liable to be rejected.

3

entities.text: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Yet, another contention raised by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Prohibition &
Excise is that, when the Act is silent for granting specific time for submitting explanation to the show cause notice, the respondents are not expected to grant time to the satisfaction of the licensees and granting seven days time to submit explanation by the petitioners is in compliance of Section 31(1) of the Act and the same is in accordance with law and the same cannot be violated,
consequently, on this ground of granting seven days time, the impugned orders cannot be set-aside.

Yet another contention raised by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Prohibition & Excise is that the fourth respondent followed the procedure strictly, contemplated under the Rules, 2017 and absolutely there is no minor violation of the Rules,
2017, which vitiates the entire proceedings under challenge and requested to dismiss the writ petitions.

Considering rival contentions, perusing the material available on record, the point that arise for consideration are as follows:
1.
Whether grant of seven days time for submitting explanation is a violation of any provision of the Act or the Rules framed there under.
If so, whether the orders under challenge in Rc.No.391/2019/C1 dated 27.01.2020 are vitiated by any irregularity and liable to be set-aside?

2. Whether the respondent No.4 followed the procedure prescribed under the Rules,
2017, for lifting the samples of liquor from the Bar and Restaurant of these petitioners.?
3. Whether failure to follow the procedure prescribed under the Act and Rules, 2017 is a ground to set-aside the impugned orders in these writ petitions.?
P O I N T No.1:
One of the ground urged before this Court is that the third respondent issued show cause notice calling for explanation of these petitioners within seven days from the date of service of notice.
Proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act mandates providing an opportunity to make representation against the action proposed.
Thus, this proviso embodied principle of natural justice.

Therefore, the authorities under the Excise Act are required to afford an opportunity to the petitioners submit their representations against the proposed action of either suspension or cancellation of 2B License.

In MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 compliance of the proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act, the third respondent issued show cause notices to the petitioners on 27.01.2020, calling upon the petitioners to submit their explanation within seven days, since, no specific time was fixed under the proviso, except affording an opportunity, grant of seven days time is sufficient to submit their explanation.

But,
the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that, atleast fifteen days time is required to be granted while calling for explanation of these petitioners in P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/
4 exercise of power under proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act.

entities.text: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Undisputedly, only seven days time is granted for submitting explanation by these petitioners.

But,
they did not submit any explanation to the notice with an intention to submit the same at the end of the month, but, in the meanwhile, the impugned orders dated 27.01.2020 were passed by the third respondent.

The, learned counsel for the petitioners Sri O. Manohar Reddy contended that atleast 15 days time is to be granted before passing any order of suspension by relying on the judgment of the learned Single Judge of High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh3, where the High Court held that, 15 days time is reasonable time for submitting an explanation from the date of service of notice when an action is proposed to be taken either for suspension or cancellation.

entities.text: High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the principle referred supra, fifteen days time is just and reasonable.
But in the present facts of the case, the respondents granted only seven days time, which is contrary to the principle laid down in the above judgment.

The proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act, clearly shows that no such license or permit shall be cancelled or suspended unless the 2013 (6) ALD 247 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 holder thereof is given an opportunity of making his representation against the action proposed.
In the present case, admittedly, the respondents issued seven days notice and afforded an opportunity to the petitioners.

A similar issue was decided by the Division Bench of the High Court of Andhra Pradesh earlier, wherein it was held that an order of suspension passed without giving notice and opportunity to the licensee is illegal and liable to be set aside.
Under these circumstances, the impugned order of suspension was set aside, by leaving it open to the first respondent to issue show cause notice to the petitioner and proceed in accordance with law.
(vide. Sri Venkateshwara Wines v. Superintendent of Prohibition and Excise, Nizamabad and others4).

entities.text: Sri Venkateshwara Wines v. Superintendent of Prohibition and Excise, Nizamabad and others4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, in the present facts of the case, show cause notices were issued to these petitioners on 27.01.2020 affording an opportunity to them to make representations as required under the proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act against the proposed action.

Therefore, on the ground that no opportunity was afforded to these petitioners, the impugned orders cannot be reversed or set-aside, however, on the ground of not affording sufficient opportunity, the order can be set- aside.

No doubt, in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh case (referred supra), the learned Single Judge held that, 15 days time is reasonable time for submitting an explanation from the date of service of notice when an action is proposed to be taken either for suspension or cancellation.

entities.text: N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Still, it is a good law, since the learned Government Pleader for Prohibition & Excise did not bring to the notice of this Court any other judgment after N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh case (referred supra).

entities.text: N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When once the seven 2004 (4) ALD 681 MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 days notice was given to these petitioners contrary to the judgment in N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh case (referred supra), it is an irregularity committed by the respondents in suspending Form-2B License of these petitioners by exercising power under Section 31(1) of the Act.

entities.text: N. Malla Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the point is answered.
P O I N T Nos. 2 & 3:

In view of the findings recorded on Point No.1, no findings need be recorded in Point Nos. 2 & 3, since such findings will have its bearing on disposal of show cause notice P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap on 11 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16823265/
5 and explanation to be submitted to the show cause notice, if any, and decision thereon.

entities.text: P. Vasanth Reddy, vs The State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, no finding is recorded in Point Nos. 2 & 3.
In view of my foregoing discussion, I find that the show cause notices issued to these petitioners in Rc.No.391/2019/C1 dated 27.01.2020 without affording sufficient opportunity is an illegality.

In the result, both the writ petitions are allowed, setting aside the show cause notices in Rc.No.391/2019/C1 dated 27.01.2020 and suspension of Form 2B License consequent thereto issued against these petitioners in both the writ petitions.

However, the respondents are at liberty to take appropriate action by issuing show cause notices to the petitioners afresh, granting fifteen (15)
days time to them.
No costs.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE M. SATYANARAYANA MURTHY Date:11.03.2020

In MSM,J W.P.Nos. 2259 & 2273 OF 2020 compliance of the proviso to Section 31(1) of the Act, the third respondent issued show cause notices to the petitioners on 27.01.2020, calling upon the petitioners to submit their explanation within seven days, since, no specific time was fixed under the proviso, except affording an opportunity, grant of seven days time is sufficient to submit their explanation.
